name: AI Index 2026 — report QA
description: Grounded QA over the AI Index 2026 corpus ingested into Qdrant: 4 happy-path questions spanning the report (capability frontier, the US-China gap, healthcare, responsible AI), scored by the LLM-judge criteria in test_config.json (final_response_match_v2 + hallucinations_v1). Kept deliberately small so routine judge runs do not exhaust API/quota.

parts.text: What does the report say about the state of AI capability in 2025?

According to the AI Index 2026 report, AI capability is accelerating rather than plateauing: industry produced over 90% of notable frontier models in 2025, and several now meet or exceed human baselines on PhD-level science questions, multimodal reasoning, and competition mathematics.

args.query: state of AI capability frontier models 2025

parts.text: What does the report say about the gap between U.S. and Chinese AI models?

The report says the U.S.–China model performance gap has effectively closed. The two have traded the lead since early 2025 — DeepSeek-R1 briefly matched the top U.S. model in February 2025 — and as of March 2026 the leading U.S. (Anthropic) model leads by just 2.7%.

args.query: US China AI model performance gap

parts.text: How is AI affecting clinical care according to the report?

The report says AI is transforming clinical care but rigorous evidence is still limited. AI tools that auto-generate clinical notes saw substantial adoption in 2025, with physicians reporting up to 83% less time spent writing notes.

args.query: AI clinical care notes physicians time

parts.text: Is responsible AI keeping pace with AI capability?

No — the report finds responsible AI is not keeping pace with capability: reporting on responsible-AI benchmarks remains spotty even though almost all frontier developers report capability benchmarks, and documented AI incidents rose sharply.
